description: Chapters 1-2 and the city: realistic tower exterior (fluted extruded fins, bevelled slabs, bronze physical glass with dusk env, amenity bands at L12/L38, crown louvres, travertine podium, cantilever canopy with soffit lights, landscaped garden court with instanced procedural trees, hedges, reflecting pool, bollards), ground (textured road, kerbs, footpath, street lamps, reflective river with ripple normal map, embankments and promenade lights), skyline (west-view sightline wedge so the river is visible from the balcony = review finding F2 root cause, two building geometries, facades reflect sky), and the lobby (no reception desk per verbatim copy; refined travertine/oak/lift cores, coffered ceiling, sculptural globe pendant, boucle chairs + olive linen sofa on wool rug, travertine drum table, olive trees in planters, low console). Depends on FEAT-001 (materials, textures, geometry-kit, envDusk). Independent of FEAT-003. Detail: plan.md '3D realism upgrade' item 2.

acceptance_criteria: build passes; scene chunk within 680 kB / 175 kB gzip
Chapter 1 and 2 screenshots show fluted fins, canopy, trees, and lobby lounge furniture with no reception desk and no floating geometry
Chapters 1 and 2 each render with <= 250 draw calls
verification: Open regenerated chapter-01/02 PNGs under C:\Users\dusitm\Desktop\Test-Kiro\tessera-sathorn\screenshots\desktop-1440 and desktop-1920 and inspect them
findings: SIZES: build OK, dist\assets\scene-*.js 624.53 kB raw / 163.58 kB gzip (FEAT-001 570.7/145.5, budget 680/175; ExtrudeGeometry/Shape/Tube/Lathe code accounts for most of the growth). TESTS: unit 7 files / 66 tests pass (63 + skyline-sightline 3). e2e 42/42 pass (8.3 min incl. a temporary render-info spec that was deleted afterwards). DRAW CALLS (window.__tessera.renderInfo(), SwiftShader, identical at 1280/1440/1920; includes the shadow pass): ch1 124 calls / 307k tris, ch2 121 / 293k, ch3 59 / 76k, ch4 47 / 76k. Budget 250. data-scene-ready: 8.8 s single worker, 12.7-14.5 s with 2 parallel workers (20 s limit; was ~8-10 s) - keep FEAT-003 start-up work modest. A first pass was 478k tris; cut by building flutes/louvres from explicit polylines (absarc/absellipse emit 24 pts), slats roundedBox segments 1, cushions segments 10, kerbs +/-600 m. INDEX.JS: createSkyline(lighting.envDusk); tower glow = exterior.userData.glowMaterials, intensity = (mat.userData.glowBase ?? 0.5) * (1 + 1.2k) (= old 0.5 + 0.6k); skyline glow = skyline.userData.glowMaterials at 0.3 + 0.9k. createSkyline now returns a Group (2 InstancedMeshes, plain + setback). Exported pure placeBlocks(rand), inWestWedge(x,z), wedgeCap(d) from skyline.js. NEW SHARED HELPERS: geometry-kit.js worldBox(w,h,d,{uvScale=1,u0,v0,flip}) (box with UVs in metres; flip = book-match) and taperedTube(points, r0, r1, tubeOpts); sets/helpers.js instancedGeometry(geometry, material, [{x,y,z,ry?,s?}], {cast,receive}) and cladPanels(batcher, material, {axis:'x'|'z'|'y', at, dir, a0,a1, b0,b1, pw, ph, gap, t, uvScale}, rand) (stone/tile panels with open joints, book-matched columns). FURNITURE LIBRARY (src/scene/furniture, no DOM, all via Batcher, each returns a Group based at y=0 with userData.furniture=true, front = +z): util.js T(x,y,z,rx,ry,rz,s)->Matrix4 and assemble(name, batcher, mats, {decal:[w,d]|null, cast=true, mount}) (adds the contact-shadow decal, tags furniture/mount) - FEAT-003 should reuse these. seating.js modularSofa(mats, {length=2.4, depth=0.95, fabric=mats.linenOlive, base=mats.walnut}) (plinth, upholstered base, arms, back frame, round(inner/0.72) seat + back cushions via cushion(), back tilted 12 deg; FEAT-003 can add arm bolsters); boucleChair(mats, {fabric=mats.boucle, base=mats.walnut}) (tub chair, extruded arc back). tables.js drumTable(mats, {radius=0.45, height=0.38, material=mats.travertine}). decor.js rug(mats, {w=3.2, d=2.4}) (12 mm, cast false, userData.top = 0.012: place items on the rug at y + top so their decals are not hidden), vase(mats, {profile=VASE_PROFILES.amphora|bottle|bowl, material=mats.ceramic, scale=1}), plantedTree(mats, {planterProfile=PLANTER_PROFILES.drum|bowl, planter=mats.travertine, height=3, seed}) (lathe planter, soil, tapered trunk + branches, 9 x 160 seeded leaves; crown reaches ~0.28*height + 0.19*height from the trunk, keep that clear of walls), PLANTER_PROFILES/VASE_PROFILES exported. lighting.js globePendant(mats, {count=9, drop=2.8, spread=0.75, seed}) - origin on the ceiling plane, hangs -y, userData.mount='ceiling', no decal, cast false. LOBBY layout: floor top y=0.1, ceiling underside 6.95, lounge centred (-1.2, 6.8) in a coffer; console x 0.2..2.6 on the slat wall between two olive trees; bench (-6, 5.0); 3 PointLights at (-6,6.2,7.5) 24, (-1.2,4.3,6.8) 9, (5,6.2,6.5) 24. No reception desk. DEVIATIONS: coffer beams are merged in the plaster Batcher rather than instanced (0 extra draw calls); river water sits at y -1.2 between the embankments and the paving is split around the channel (no coplanar overlap -> no z-fighting at 700 m); court/road/park overlays use polygonOffset; river material is a clone of mats.river (keeps envDusk) with the specified colour/roughness/normalMap/envMapIntensity. VISUAL CHECK (desktop-1440 ch1/ch2, desktop-1920 ch1, plus 1440 ch4): fluted fins, slab lines, canopy with bronze fascia and soffit lights, trees and hedges read; lobby shows coffered ceiling, LED cove, travertine-panelled cores with bronze portals and two-leaf doors, globe pendant, olive linen sofa, two boucle chairs on the wool rug, console with ceramic vessels between two olive trees; no floating geometry, z-fighting or shadow acne seen. Ch4 (still the FEAT-001 residence) now shows the river as a light reflective band with promenade lights. STILL IMPERFECT: the drum table is mostly hidden behind the chairs from the ch2 camera; the canopy/entrance and amenity bands are small at ch1 distance (the L12/L38 recesses are faint); the east face is in shadow so its fins read flat; per spec the west wedge has no blocks beyond 540 m, so the far bank of the river is empty ground; street-lamp poles near the ch1 camera show as thin diagonal lines in the foreground.
